sentences.text: Brachydeirus was a small to moderately large arthrodire placoderm that lived in Europe during the Late Devonian. Living animals would have looked superficially like modern trout or small mackerels.
These species had a highly compressed body in cross-section, a pointed snout, and very large orbits.
The genus is distinguished by a median dorsal plate on its trunk shield that is often keeled with a high, prominent ridge.
In Brachydeirus carinatus, the dermal bones are decorated with large tubercles arranged in concentric circles.
Conversely, the dermal bones of Brachydeirus grandis feature small, evenly spaced tubercles.
Brachydeirus magnus displays a dermal surface covered in very large tubercles.
Brachydeirus gracilis is the smallest species in the genus, with a holotype skull length of only 6 cm.
At the other end of the size spectrum, Brachydeirus grandis is one of the largest species, with a holotype skull length of around 20 cm.
Brachydeirus magnus is a very large species that was originally described as a specimen of Anomalichthys.
The genus Brachydeirus was first described by Koenen in 1880.
Fossils of this genus are restricted to the Kellwasserkalk Fauna found at Bad Wildungen and Adorf.
Brachydeirus carinatus possesses a broad nuchal plate that curves outward at the back.
Brachydeirus grandis has an unusually long lateral trunk shield and relatively small orbits compared to other species.
Brachydeirus has been known by the synonyms Brachydirus, Anomalichthys (in part), and Auchenosteus.
The type species of the genus Brachydeirus is Brachydeirus carinatus.
Six species are recognized within the genus: B. bicarinatus, B. carinatus, B. gracilis, B. grandis, B. magnus, and B. minor.
The parent group of the genus is the family Brachydeiridae.
Brachydeirus belongs to the class Placodermi.
Brachydeirus lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
